A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same cognitive framework and LearnArena benchmark. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting and additional material in v2.

before.justification: V1 reports original instructor-learning, concept-learning, experience-learning and LearnArena experiments, plus appendix results on knowledge selection.

after.justification: V2 retains these empirical results and adds alternative-opponent evaluations and GPT-4o-mini many-shot results in Appendices B–C.

M1.justification: The three learning procedures, LearnArena feedback and experience-selection process, training approach and prompt templates remain unchanged. The new discussion of self-critique explains the framework's scope without introducing an implemented method component.

E1.justification: The mathematical, non-mathematical, competitive-game, logic and planning coverage is retained. The added experiments reuse MagpieMath and four existing LearnArena games; their differences concern model and opponent configurations rather than new datasets or task requirements.

E2.justification: Appendix C newly includes GPT-4o-mini in the many-shot evaluation, although this model already appeared in v1's LearnArena comparisons. Existing comparator sets in the original experiments remain intact. Appendix B uses six existing learner models against alternative opponents.

E3.justification: Appendix B adds comparisons with three alternative fixed opponents, aggregating four-game scores for six learners. Appendix C adds a GPT-4o-mini 128k-context evaluation through 100 examples with a four-shot reference. A.1 also states 20 runs per task, differing from the retained 20-matches-per-model–environment description; the PDFs do not establish a rerun.

E4.justification: New Appendix B directly investigates benchmark sensitivity to opponent choice using Phi-4, GPT-4o-mini and GPT-4o. Appendix C extends the many-shot robustness analysis to GPT-4o-mini. These add substantive validation beyond the retained instructor-scaling and knowledge-selection analyses, which were already present in v1.

E5.justification: V2 A.1 newly specifies 20 independent runs for each task, changing the granularity of LearnArena's repetition information without clearly establishing increased runs. Both versions retain 20-seed ICL experiments with means and standard deviations. Appendix B's proposed future variance reporting is not an implemented uncertainty analysis.

E6.justification: Tables 3–5 add opponent-specific win rates, and Appendix B reports ranking correlations of 1.000, 0.829 and 0.714. Appendix C adds GPT-4o-mini accuracies, peaking at 75.2 at 15 shots and reaching 70.6 at 100 shots. Original result tables and plots are retained; Section 7 corrects GPT-4o's stated average from 0.70 to Table 2's unchanged 0.75.

T1.justification: Equation (1), the task tuple and the instructional, conceptual and experiential context definitions are retained. Appendix D restates existing mathematics; the added conceptual explanations introduce no new theorem, proof or formal derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: the three-part cognitive framework, findings about interaction, scale and many-shot limitations, and LearnArena. Additional supporting experiments do not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: Appendices B–F add substantive explanations of opponent sensitivity, long-context capacity versus many-shot generalization, instructional guidance versus raw experience, dataset selection and self-critique's place in the framework. V2 also acknowledges that win rate is a coarse learning measure and proposes future process metrics. The earlier limitations paragraph is retained.

D1.justification: V2 adds a public LearnArena code-access pointer, 50-task-per-environment information, average input-token lengths and an illustrative game-history log in Figure 11; the anonymous dataset pointer is removed. Hardware, training hyperparameters, corpus counts and existing prompt templates remain unchanged. These are documentation changes, not evidence of altered implementation.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations including RecAI, RecExplainer, GuardReasoner, GVPO and RSPO. Appendix C expands discussion of Agarwal et al.'s many-shot findings, while Appendix F relates self-critique to the proposed taxonomy. The central novelty positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Most existing prose is retained with limited copyediting. Instructor scaling moves from Appendix B to Section 4.3, and benchmark correlations move from Section 7 to Appendix A.6. V2 adds explanatory appendices, acknowledgments and a conference checklist, and removes the standalone Impact Statements section.

P2.justification: The two-column main paper becomes a single-column NeurIPS document, extensively changing text flow, display sizing and table placement. Existing figures are relocated or renumbered with their graphics retained. Three opponent-result tables and the Figure 11 game-history display are added.

improvement.justification: V2 adds useful validation of opponent dependence and many-shot behavior, and clarifies the framework's distinctions and measurement limitations. These targeted additions improve empirical support and interpretability. The gain is qualified by unresolved reproducibility ambiguity: A.1's 50 tasks with 20 runs each is not reconciled with Section 7's retained 20-match description.
